Great Journeys

A Every summer, millions of people go away on holiday with a passport, a suitcase and a phone in their pocket. They book a hotel online and arrive in a few hours. But travel wasn't always so easy — and some of the greatest journeys happened long before there were planes.

B In 1325 a young man from Tangier, in Morocco, set off for Mecca to go on the Hajj. His name was Ibn Battuta, and he was 21. He didn't come home for 24 years. He travelled through North Africa, the Middle East and Central Asia — he visited Bukhara and Samarkand — and went as far as India and China: more than 100,000 kilometres. When he came home, he told his stories to a writer, who wrote them down in a famous book, the Rihla. Some historians think that he didn't really visit every place in it.

C In 1841 an Englishman, Thomas Cook, organised a train trip for about 500 people from Leicester to Loughborough, a town 11 miles away. Each passenger paid one shilling. The trip was a great success, and Cook started a business that sold tickets and hotels together — the first package holidays. In 1872 he even took a group of tourists around the world.

D In 1889 an American journalist, Nellie Bly, decided to travel around the world faster than Phileas Fogg, the hero of Jules Verne's novel Around the World in Eighty Days. She took only one small bag, and she travelled by ship and by train. In France she met Jules Verne himself. She got back to New York 72 days after she left.

E In 1950 there were about 25 million international tourist trips in the world. In 2024 there were about 1.4 billion, according to UN Tourism.

F Most of us will never travel like Ibn Battuta. But every great journey began in the same way: somebody packed a bag and set off.

2

Grammar · past simple

TUSHUNTIRISH — PAST SIMPLE

A Tasdiq. Toʻgʻri feʼllarga -ed qoʻshiladi: visit → visited · arrive → arrived. Koʻp ishlatiladigan feʼllarning aksariyati notoʻgʻri: go → went · take → took · buy → bought · leave → left · fly → flew.

B Inkor va soʻroq — did / didn't + feʼlning oddiy shakli: He didn't come home for 24 years. · Did you have a good time? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. · Where did you go?

C was / were bilan did ishlatilmaydi: The trip was a success. · We weren't tired. · Were you late? Vaqt soʻzlari: yesterday · last summer · in 1889 · two years ago — ago vaqtdan keyin keladi.

D Istisnolar. did / didn't dan keyin feʼl oddiy shaklga qaytadi: Did you go? — Did you went? emas. Imlo: stop → stopped · plan → planned · travel → travelled (harf ikkilanadi) · study → studied, lekin play → played.

4 ✗ We was very tired. → ✓ We were … · ✗ I buyed a hat. → ✓ I bought …

5 ✗ I went there before two years. → ✓ two years ago

Vocabulary · tourism

3.1 Read Javohir's post. Look at the phrases in bold.

OUR FIRST TRIP ABROAD

Last summer my cousin and I went away on holiday to Germany. First we got visas at the embassy in Tashkent — that took three weeks! Then we booked our accommodation online and exchanged some money: you need euros, the foreign currency there. I packed a big suitcase; my cousin only took a backpack. In Berlin we checked into a cheap hostel, unpacked our luggage and did some sightseeing with a guidebook and a paper map. On the last day we bought souvenirs for the whole family, checked out of the hostel and spent our last night on a campsite near a lake. It wasn't a luxury holiday, but we had a real adventure. Next time I'll pack suntan lotion and sunglasses — it was 35 degrees!

5

Everyday English · asking for information

TUSHUNTIRISH — MAʼLUMOT SOʻRASH

A Maʼlumot soʻrash: What time's the next train? · How often do the trains leave? · Which platform does it leave from? · How much is a ticket? · Can I pay by card? · Where can I buy a magazine?

B Sizga yordam beradigan odam: How can I help you? · Is there anything else I can help you with? Yana soʻrash: Sorry, just one more thing. · Actually, there is one more thing.

C Xushmuomalaroq: Could you tell me where the ticket office is? Could you tell me … dan keyin soʻz tartibi savoldagidek emas: where the ticket office is — where is the ticket office emas.

D Istisno. do / does / did ham tushib qoladi: What time does the museum open? → Could you tell me what time the museum opens?
